steps.label: research:help-flag.0

return.plan:
Give `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs` two help flags on its existing dispatch switch, and leave every other path byte-identical.

The file already has exactly one dispatch point: `const [command, ...rest] = process.argv.slice(2)` at line 492, followed by `switch (command)` at line 498 whose `default` is `fail(command ? `unknown command "${command}"\n${USAGE}` : USAGE, 2)`. `fail(message, code)` (line 70) writes `message + '\n'` to stderr and exits with `code`. So the usage text already reaches stderr with a trailing newline on both wrong-call paths, and nothing else in the file reads `process.argv`.

Two changes, both small.

1. Add a case pair to that switch, immediately before `default`:

```
  case '--help':
  case '-h':
    process.stdout.write(USAGE + '\n')
    break
```

The script ends after the switch, so falling out of it exits 0 with no explicit `process.exit`. Write `USAGE + '\n'` and not `USAGE` alone: that makes the help output byte-identical to the text `fail` puts on stderr, which is what lets the suite pin the two paths against each other. Do not call `need()` here — help takes no arguments, and arguments after the flag are ignored the way the flag itself is ignored after a command word.

Put a two-sentence comment above the pair, in the prose style the rest of the file uses, saying why the same text is stdout-and-0 here and stderr-and-2 in `default`: asking for the calling convention is a successful call, being called wrongly is not, and a caller has to be able to tell them apart by exit code alone.

2. Append one line to the `USAGE` array (line 53-64), after the `read` entry:

```
  '  backlog.mjs --help',
```

The issue's complaint is that the calling convention is only discoverable by provoking an error; a usage block that does not mention the flag leaves half of that standing. It costs nothing on the error path, which prints the same array.

Touch nothing else in the file. In particular the `default` branch, `fail`, and the bare-invocation behaviour (`command` undefined, so `fail(USAGE, 2)`) stay exactly as they are — criterion 3 is satisfied by not editing them, and the suite pins that.

Rejected alternatives:
- Intercepting the flags before the switch with an early `process.stdout.write(...)` and `process.exit(0)`. It puts a second dispatch point beside the switch and an explicit exit where no other command has one; the switch already is the dispatcher.
- A `help` subcommand word, or making a bare invocation print help and exit 0. The criteria name `--help` and `-h`; a bare call is a wrong call and keeps exit 2, and changing it would silently reclassify an existing error.
- Routing help through `fail(USAGE, 0)`. `fail` writes to stderr by definition and its comment defines exit 2 and exit 1 as the two wrong-call codes; help is neither.
- Scanning all of `process.argv` for the flags so `backlog.mjs index -h <path>` would also print help. Nothing asks for it, and it would put a flag scan in front of arguments that are legitimately file paths.

Style of the file: two-space indent, single quotes, no semicolons, comments as prose paragraphs above the thing they explain. Match it; the test file next door uses semicolons and that is its own convention, not this file's.

Documentation: `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md` shows only the `start` and `record` invocations and enumerates no subcommand list, so it needs no change. `skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md` describes the suite and does need one — the test-author owns that edit as part of its step.

This is the only file the production change touches.

return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. Three new cases prove the criteria and a fourth guards the behaviour the change is most likely to break by accident. All four go in `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs`, the existing `node:test` suite, and are run with `node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs` from the repository root.

The suite doc at `skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md` is present and accurate; load it and follow it for naming, fixtures and faked-vs-real. Two things in it are contradicted by this work and you correct them as part of your step, along with the ordinary 'what the suite covers' extension:
- Its `runAsync` entry says 'The last case uses this and never `run()`', framing the helper as existing for the collector case alone. These cases use `runAsync` too, for the reason given below, so that framing has to change.
- Its 'Where a new case belongs' sentence lists the file's block order; add the help-flag block to it where you place it.

Why `runAsync` and not `run`: `run()` returns stdout only, and `execFileSync` lets the child's stderr through to the parent's stderr rather than capturing it, so a case asserting that help writes nothing to stderr cannot be written with it. `runAsync(args, cleanEnv())` resolves to `{ stdout, stderr }` and rejects on a non-zero exit, so awaiting it is itself the exit-0 assertion. Pass `cleanEnv()` explicitly, as every other spawn in the file does. Do not add a new helper for this; do not touch `run`, `runFails` or `runAsync` themselves.

Placement: these are argument-handling cases that belong to no single subcommand, which the doc calls shared mechanics. Put the block after the `read` cases and before the atomic-`.tmp` case, under a short comment saying they are the CLI's own argument handling rather than one command's rules.

The cases.

1. Criterion 1 — `--help` prints the usage to stdout and exits 0.
   Level: end to end, the real CLI as a child process, like every other case.
   Setup: a fresh `tmpDir()`, no backlog file, no init — help must need no state at all.
   Call: `await runAsync(['--help'], cleanEnv())`.
   Expect: it resolves, which is exit 0. `stdout` starts with `'usage:\n'`. `stdout` contains a line for each of the nine subcommands — assert on `'backlog.mjs init'`, `'backlog.mjs start'`, `'backlog.mjs record'`, `'backlog.mjs branch'`, `'backlog.mjs close'`, `'backlog.mjs index'`, `'backlog.mjs steps'`, `'backlog.mjs codemap'`, `'backlog.mjs read'`, and on `'--help'`. `stderr` is `''`. And the temp directory is still empty (`fs.readdirSync(dir)` deep-equals `[]`) — asking for the usage writes no file and creates no backlog.

2. Criterion 2 — `-h` behaves exactly like `--help`.
   Same level and setup. Run both flags in this one case and compare: the two stdout strings are strictly equal, `-h`'s stderr is `''`, and `-h` resolves (exit 0). Byte equality is the assertion; do not re-list the usage lines here.

3. Criterion 3 — an unknown command keeps exiting 2 with the usage on stderr.
   Call `runFails(['wat'])` for the failure, and `await runAsync(['--help'], cleanEnv())` in the same case for the reference text.
   Expect: `err.status` is `2`; `err.stdout || ''` is `''` — the usage must not have moved to stdout on the error path; and `err.stderr` is strictly equal to `'unknown command "wat"\n' + help.stdout`. That last equality is the point of the case: it pins that both paths print the same usage text and that only the stream and the exit code differ.

4. Guard, not a criterion — a call with no arguments at all keeps exiting 2 with the usage on stderr. A naive help implementation tends to sweep the bare invocation into the success path, which would reclassify an existing error as an exit 0. Call `runFails([])`; expect `err.status` is `2`, `err.stdout || ''` is `''`, and `err.stderr` is strictly equal to the `--help` stdout (the bare path prints `USAGE` with no leading line). Reuse the reference text the way case 3 does.

Deliberately untested:
- `--help` or `-h` followed by extra arguments. The plan ignores them and nothing depends on the behaviour, so pinning it would freeze an accident.
- The flags in a non-leading position, such as `index -h <path>`. They are recognised only as the command word by design; a case here would demand a flag scan the plan rejects.
- Every other subcommand's behaviour. None of them is touched, and the existing cases already cover them.

What counts as done — the closed list, from the repository root:

    node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs

Nothing else is run: no `test.sh`, no other suite, no linter (there is none).

What is already red: I ran nothing, not even a baseline — a run buys no fact here that reading the file did not already give. Expect the existing 1026-line suite to be green as it stands, and expect the four new cases to fail before `backlog.mjs` is changed: cases 1 and 2 because the flags currently fall into `default` and exit 2 with stderr, case 3 because its reference `--help` call fails the same way, and case 4 for the same reason. Case 4's assertion about the bare call is the only one whose subject already behaves correctly.
return.summary: Planned the help flags for the backlog CLI: a `case '--help': case '-h':` pair on the existing dispatch switch that writes the usage plus a newline to stdout and falls out of the switch at exit 0, plus a `--help` line appended to the usage block, with the unknown-command path left untouched. Four end-to-end cases in the existing suite pin the two flags byte-identical to each other, the error path's usage byte-identical to the help output on stderr at exit 2, and the bare invocation still an error.
